statement_timeout_why.text: EP-D17 (WF3, 2026-09-10, C1; output-panel fix F4) — declared "none" DELIBERATELY, not a hardcoded duration: this entry inherits step_post_check_statement_timeout_minutes (10 min default) as its ceiling, resolved by scripts/lib/step/index.js at run time. A hardcoded "10m" literal here would have won over the tunable and made step_post_check_statement_timeout_minutes inert (Rule 3 — nothing hidden). Cloud EXPLAIN measured this SQL shape (a full Seq Scan on parcels, cost 568,601-573,235) at 16-30s on a vacuumed heap vs 40+ min against the 1,346,759 dead tuples pass 4 creates — the 10-minute default is 20-37x the clean-heap cost with headroom, and raising the tunable (not editing this entry) is how an operator widens it.

why.text: EP-D17 (WF3, 2026-09-10, C4) — operator structural ruling: bloat maintenance is part of the STANDARD step, not chain-tail folklore. Output-panel fix F2/F3 (2026-09-10): the caller (scripts/lib/step/index.js) runs execution.maintenance's runMaintenance BEFORE this entry, not after — an earlier draft had this reading the PRE-vacuum state on every run, which would WARN by construction (0.697 measured, well above the 0.30 default) and degrade every healthy chain to completed_with_warnings. With the reorder, THIS row reads the POST-maintenance state: on a run where the target exceeded the threshold, runMaintenance has already VACUUMed it, so a healthy run reads near 0, not 0.697.
